challenge.title: A hot feed stops forever after one outage
challenge.prompt: Review where exceptions are handled relative to sharing and how a later retry can restart the producer.

snippet.context: ViewModel properties. refreshes is MutableStateFlow<Int> with initial 0; repository.observeFeed is a cold Flow<List<Item>>, Ui.Content and Ui.Failed model renderable state. Retry is a user action.
dependencies: AndroidX lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx where ViewModel scope is used

correctedImplementation.context: ViewModel properties. refreshes is MutableStateFlow<Int> with initial 0; repository.observeFeed is a cold Flow<List<Item>>, Ui.Content and Ui.Failed model renderable state. Retry is a user action.
dependencies: AndroidX lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx where ViewModel scope is used

issues.rootCause: Upstream failure terminates the sharing job; StateFlow does not relay it to downstream catch.
issues.consequence: UI can remain stuck on the last value with no error state.

issues.rootCause: A one-shot fallback completes the failed upstream.
issues.consequence: A retry button cannot restore collection by merely re-observing the same StateFlow.
issues.fix: Restart an inner producer from an explicit refresh trigger.

challenge.tradeoffs: Preserve cached content alongside a recoverable error in a real offline-first screen. Automatically retry only classified transient errors with bounds; a user trigger should not become an uncontrolled parallel request fan-out.
followUps: What happens when the app goes invisible and then gains a new collector?

challenge.title: A native module leaks work after its React instance closes
challenge.prompt: Review native work ownership, main-thread blocking, and promise failure behavior during module invalidation.

snippet.context: React Native TurboModule implementation. NativeCacheSpec is Codegen-generated with read(key, Promise); DiskCache.read is a custom blocking method. Constructor receives app context and cache. Use kotlinx.coroutines and java.io.IOException.

correctedImplementation.context: React Native TurboModule implementation. NativeCacheSpec is Codegen-generated with read(key, Promise); DiskCache.read is a custom blocking method. Constructor receives app context and cache. Use kotlinx.coroutines and java.io.IOException.

issues.rootCause: The React instance may be destroyed before the job ends.
issues.consequence: The job retains resources and can attempt delivery into a dead runtime.
issues.fix: Own a module scope and cancel it from invalidate.

issues.rootCause: The suspend wrapper does not change the blocking call’s execution thread.
issues.consequence: Native UI stalls during disk access.
issues.fix: Perform blocking storage work on IO.

issues.rootCause: Expected IO failure never settles the live caller’s promise.
issues.consequence: JS can wait indefinitely and unhandled errors can crash.
issues.fix: Map expected failures to stable rejection codes while preserving cancellation.

challenge.tradeoffs: A destroyed JS runtime cannot be promised a final callback, and coroutine cancellation does not interrupt every blocking API. Bound the cache operation and validate keys at the native boundary. Do not cache an Activity in a process- or module-owned object.
followUps: How would you prevent a multi-callback SDK from settling the same Promise twice?

challenge.title: Supervision still cancels the useful panel
challenge.prompt: Explain why supervision alone does not preserve optional-failure behavior when await throws out of the block.

snippet.context: Repository operation. profile is required; recommendations are optional and may fail with IOException. Screen takes Profile and List<Recommendation>.

correctedImplementation.context: Repository operation. profile is required; recommendations are optional and may fail with IOException. Screen takes Profile and List<Recommendation>.

issues.rootCause: A supervised async stores failure, but await still throws.
issues.consequence: The supervisor block fails instead of returning a usable required result.
issues.fix: Convert only the expected optional failure into a domain fallback.

issues.rootCause: Supervision is treated as error handling.
issues.consequence: A valid partial response is lost and cancellation can be accidentally swallowed by a broad fallback.
issues.fix: Keep required failure fatal and preserve cancellation in optional handling.

challenge.tradeoffs: An empty optional panel is only acceptable under the stated product policy; a typed unavailable panel often communicates better. Required profile failure still cancels the overall operation.
followUps: Why would adding CoroutineExceptionHandler to async not implement this fallback?

challenge.title: An old account’s refresh appears after logout
challenge.prompt: Review identity capture across suspension and isolation of local reads/writes when accounts switch.

snippet.context: Repository. activeAccount is StateFlow<String?>. api.fetch(accountId) and dao.replaceForAccount/observeForAccount use explicit account partitions. Anonymous state should render an empty list. Item is immutable.

correctedImplementation.context: Repository. activeAccount is StateFlow<String?>. api.fetch(accountId) and dao.replaceForAccount/observeForAccount use explicit account partitions. Anonymous state should render an empty list. Item is immutable.

issues.rootCause: A response requested for account A commits after switching to B into shared storage.
issues.consequence: A different user may see private cached data.
issues.fix: Capture request identity and partition both persistence and observation by account.

issues.rootCause: Logout is a normal concurrent state transition.
issues.consequence: The refresh can crash or use an invalid session.
issues.fix: Exit gracefully when no account is active; authentication must also be enforced by the API.

challenge.tradeoffs: Partitioning permits an old request to update only its own account cache; retaining that cache after logout is a separate explicit security policy. If logout must erase it, coordinate generation checks and deletion atomically so an in-flight write cannot recreate it.
followUps: How would you test rapid A-to-B-to-A switching and enforce server-side authorization?
